context: Changes normalize_path to return Cow<str> so already-normalized paths skip allocation.
explanation: Most paths flowing through this function have no backslashes or double slashes, so the old code unconditionally allocated a new String via .replace() even when nothing needed to change. The Cow<str> version returns a borrowed slice of the original input in the common case and only allocates when a rewrite is actually needed, while staying ergonomic since Cow derefs to &str and callers needing an owned String can call .into_owned().
